original_source_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-flat-finitely-presented-permanence-algebra}
Let $R \to A \to B$ be ring maps.
Assume $R \to B$ is of finite presentation and
$A \to B$ faithfully flat and of finite presentation.
Then $R \to A$ is of finite presentation.

final_content.statement: Let $R\to A\to B$ be homomorphisms of commutative rings. If $B$ is finitely presented as an $R$-algebra and $A\to B$ is faithfully flat and finitely presented, then $A$ is finitely presented as an $R$-algebra.
hypotheses: R→B is finitely presented; A→B faithfully flat and finitely presented.

semantic_review_note: Pinned descent.tex L4260–4266 assumes composable R→A→B, B FINITELY PRESENTED over R, and A→B FAITHFULLY FLAT AND FINITELY PRESENTED. It concludes A FINITELY PRESENTED over R, not merely finite type; the proposal retains both finite-presentation hypotheses and ring order.

original_source_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-finite-type-local-source-fppf-algebra}
Let $R \to A \to B$ be ring maps.
Assume $R \to B$ is of finite type and
$A \to B$ faithfully flat and of finite presentation.
Then $R \to A$ is of finite type.

final_content.statement: Let $R\to A\to B$ be ring homomorphisms. If $B$ is a finitely generated $R$-algebra and the map $A\to B$ is faithfully flat and of finite presentation, then $A$ is a finitely generated $R$-algebra.
hypotheses: R→B finite type; A→B faithfully flat and finite presentation.

semantic_review_note: Original L4351–4358 requires B FINITE TYPE over R, and A→B faithfully flat and of FINITE PRESENTATION. It descends FINITE TYPE to R→A; the proposed statement preserves the asymmetry between the two finiteness conditions.

final_content.statement: Let $X\xrightarrow fY\xrightarrow q S$ be morphisms of schemes, with composite $p=q\circ f$. Suppose $f:X\to Y$ is surjective, flat, and locally of finite presentation. If $p:X\to S$ is locally of finite presentation, then $q:Y\to S$ is locally of finite presentation. Separately, if $p$ is locally of finite type, then $q$ is locally of finite type.
hypotheses: f surjective flat locally finitely presented; p locally finite presentation/finite type.
conclusions: q has the same corresponding finiteness property.

semantic_review_note: Original L4384–4400 has composable schemes X→^f Y→^q S with p=q∘f and f SURJECTIVE FLAT LOCALLY FINITELY PRESENTED. It provides TWO corresponding claims: p locally of finite presentation ⇒ q locally of finite presentation, and p locally of finite type ⇒ q locally of finite type. The proposal preserves the separate weaker and stronger hypotheses.

final_content.statement: Let $X\xrightarrow fY\xrightarrow q S$ be morphisms of schemes, with composite $p=q\circ f$. In each of the following three cases, assume $f$ is surjective and has the indicated property, and $p$ has the same property: (i) both $f$ and $p$ are syntomic; (ii) both are smooth; (iii) both are étale. Then in the corresponding case $q$ is syntomic, smooth, or étale, respectively.
hypotheses: f is surjective, and f and p are both syntomic, or both smooth, or both étale.

semantic_review_note: Original L4422–4438 assumes surjective morphism f:X→Y syntomic (respectively smooth, étale) AND composite p:X→S has SAME property; it concludes q:Y→S has that property. The text preserves each of the three matched cases rather than mixing smooth p with an étale f.

final_content.statement: Let $X\xrightarrow fY\xrightarrow q S$ be morphisms of schemes, with composite $p=q\circ f$. Assume $f:X\to Y$ is surjective, flat, and locally of finite presentation and the composite $p:X\to S$ is syntomic (flat, locally finitely presented, with local complete intersection fibres). Then both $q:Y\to S$ and $f:X\to Y$ are syntomic.
hypotheses: f surjective flat lfp, and p syntomic.
conclusions: Both q and f are syntomic.

semantic_review_note: Original L4495–4512 assumes f:X→Y SURJECTIVE FLAT LOCALLY FINITELY PRESENTED and p:X→S SYNTOMIC. It concludes BOTH q:Y→S AND f:X→Y syntomic. The proposal retains simultaneous conclusions and the fpqc nature of f, not only descent of the target map.
